mappings.note: Asks for several DIFFERENT ways of producing sound, which is LO-1's 'production of sound in multiple ways ... using materials in surroundings'. Not LO-2, which is the single causal claim that vibration is the cause; here the cause is assumed and the enumeration is the answer.

The answer is a list of vibrating PARTS: strings, air columns, membranes - the three categories LO-1 names verbatim. Not LO-73, which is about describing music in terms of loudness and pitch, neither of which this item asks for.
The reason under test is 'sound requires a medium', which is LO-4 word for word. Not LO-3: nothing here compares air with solid or liquid, the whole point is the absence of any medium.

Tests that the disturbance advances while particles only oscillate - the mechanics of LO-5's longitudinal wave. Not LO-4: a medium is present throughout; the false claim is about particle motion, not about necessity.

Same outcome as P4 and honestly so: LO-5 is the frame's only wave-mechanics outcome, and this item tests its other half (energy travels, matter does not). The frame offers no separate 'sound transfers energy' outcome to split them on.

Content is compression/rarefaction structure (LO-5); the task is to BUILD the density-distance graph and label its axes, which is LO-78's 'develop model to represent'. Not LO-79, which is for using a model to get a result rather than constructing one.

Frequency and time period are LO-6 characteristics. C8.2 rather than LO-79 because the item directs the student to re-run Activity 10.1 with a changed variable and infer from the observation - a plan for inquiry, not a substitution into a formula.
Pure numeric use of the definition of frequency (LO-6) to predict a count (LO-79). Not C8.2: no apparatus or procedure is involved, the piston is given.
Wavelength read off a given graph and halved - LO-6 supplies the quantity, LO-79 the use of the supplied model. Not LO-78: the graph is given, the student does not draw it.

Ratios ACROSS solid, liquid and gas, which is exactly LO-3's 'travel through different mediums (air, solid and liquid)'. LO-79 for the numeric manipulation. Chosen over LO-6 because the comparison is between states of matter, not a property of one wave.

Same steel-vs-air content as P10 (LO-3) but the question is whether Gunjan could DISTINGUISH the two arrivals - a real-life event judged against a perceptual threshold, so LO-77 rather than LO-79's plain prediction.

Echo has no learning outcome anywhere in curriculum 82's legal set for this chapter; CG2's 'scientific principles and laws' is the only honest anchor. LO-79 for applying 2d = vt to get a minimum distance.
SONAR likewise has no outcome; CG2 carries it. LO-79 for halving the round trip and computing the depth. Not LO-6: the unknown is a distance, not a wave characteristic.
Asks which OBSERVATION proves sound is mechanical, and the key is 'needs a medium' - LO-4. Not LO-5: longitudinal character is not what distinguishes mechanical from non-mechanical.

Links frequency (LO-6) to the number of COMPRESSIONS per second, so it also needs the longitudinal picture (LO-5). That pairing is what separates it from the other frequency items, which never mention compressions.
Straight arithmetic on the definition of frequency. LO-79 rather than C8.2 because no experiment is designed or observed, a count and a time are simply given.

Echo-versus-reverberation has no outcome, so CG2. LO-80 for 'justify your answer': the student must predict the perceptual outcome from the 0.1 s rule held as prior knowledge. Not LO-79, since no quantity is produced.
Compares wavelength and amplitude across two given graphs - both LO-6 characteristics - and uses the supplied model to rank them (LO-79). Not LO-78: nothing is drawn.
Frequency ordering (LO-6) but the deliverable is to MARK A, B and C onto the curves, i.e. to produce an annotated model, which is LO-78 rather than N5's read-only LO-79.
Pure construction: a graph drawn from a given amplitude and wavelength. LO-78 for the model, LO-6 for the two characteristics that fix it.
The first error is that a vacuum carries no sound (LO-4); LO-77 because the task is to analyse a depicted real-life scene and name the factors that make it wrong, including the light/sound speed gap.
v = f-lambda then T = 1/f: two LO-6 characteristics chained. LO-79 for the substitution. Not LO-3, no medium comparison is made.
SONAR depth again under CG2 for want of an outcome; LO-79 for the round-trip halving. Shares codes with P13 and honestly so - the two differ only in the numbers and the target.
Same ultrasonic-ranging gap as the SONAR items (CG2 + LO-79), but LO-77 is added because the item is framed as a vehicle parking system whose behaviour must be analysed, not a bare depth sum.
Temperature changes the SPEED within one medium, so this is LO-6's speed characteristic rather than LO-3's comparison across states of matter. LO-79 for the two-time subtraction.
